strategic_horizon.terminal_goal: Ship a personal weak-network VPN whose sustained public payload remains WBD-owned raw TCP-shaped FakeTCP -> pinned wolfSSL DTLS 1.3 -> LINK/lane-local FEC without ordinary kernel-TCP HOL, while the user-visible Logical Tunnel has a server-assigned stable address lease and may sleep, reconnect, rotate or race multiple independent transport lanes without being tied to one immortal FakeTCP 4-tuple.
strategic_horizon.current_milestone: ADR-0012 architecture pivot. Stop treating per-LiveID Linux netns + veth + double NAT as the final Windows raw-IP product. Implement Account -> Device/Installation -> Logical Tunnel -> replaceable Transport Lanes, server-assigned unique tunnel IPv4 leases, shared Linux TUN + one host NAT, and promote the existing Game Lane PacketID/first-arrival/dedup semantics into the general multipath/replacement layer.
strategic_horizon.local_optimization_stop_rule: Do not reopen the preserved hard transport/security/release constraints while performing this pivot: no ordinary kernel-TCP WBD payload path, no TCP-over-TCP HOL, per-lane same-association Reality bootstrap -> DTLS -> LINK lineage, pinned wolfSSL DTLS 1.3, legacy FakeTCP default, FEC off or fixed 20:20 with lane-local immutable state, <=100 Mbit/s weak-link qualification ceiling, 40 Mbit/s aggregate-inner conservative release point. Do not mix startup-RTT optimization or Windows child-process slimming into this work.

continuation_cursor.current_task: Immediately stop product expansion of the netns/double-NAT raw-IP architecture and begin ADR-0012 Phase 1: introduce Logical Tunnel identity distinct from LiveID/lane and add a server-assigned unique IPv4 lease/configuration model. Do not yet optimize handshake latency, refactor Windows child processes, or remove historical netns evidence.
continuation_cursor.why_now: The old netns topology existed mainly because every Windows client reused inner 10.66.0.2/30. Unique server-assigned tunnel addresses remove that collision at the correct identity layer and permit a shared TUN + one NAT. Separately, the later Game Lane code already provides the PacketID, first-arrival, duplicate suppression and no-cross-lane-HOL machinery needed for seamless make-before-break lane replacement, so creating a second migration sequencing layer would be redundant. The decisive netns product qualification had not yet run to completion, so pivoting now avoids deepening likely throwaway topology.
continuation_cursor.done_when: Phase 1 is complete when Account/Device/Logical-Tunnel/Transport-Lane ownership is explicit in code and tests, same-account concurrent logical tunnels receive distinct server-assigned IPv4 leases from a configurable pool, Windows no longer globally assumes 10.66.0.2/30, authenticated tunnel configuration carries address/prefix/route parameters, raw-IP ingress enforces source == leased IP, reconnect/cleanup/reuse semantics are deterministic, and no preserved transport/no-HOL/security/release hard constraint regresses. Then proceed to shared TUN + one host NAT.

local_test_snapshot.scope: Architecture/document/handoff pivot only. No product data-plane code was changed in this pivot set. Live Actions must be refreshed before implementation work; previously added raw-IP netns workflows were not accepted as proof of the new ADR-0012 architecture.

product_policy.public_transport: Each Transport Lane is one complete WBD-owned FakeTCP association carrying Reality-like TLS bootstrap, DTLS 1.3, LINK and lane-local FEC/payload on the same lane 4-tuple/sequence space. Ordinary kernel TCP may not become the WBD payload carrier.
product_policy.logical_tunnel: Logical Tunnel identity, server-assigned tunnel IP lease and race PacketID space survive lane rotation/reconnect/idle sleep. LiveID/FakeTCP/DTLS/LINK are disposable lane identities.
product_policy.multipath: Normal steady mode targets one lane. The later Game Lane design may use 2..4 independent complete WBD associations with first-arrival delivery and duplicate suppression. Make-before-break replacement may temporarily add a candidate lane and must rotate only one healthy game lane at a time.
product_policy.idle_rotation: Payload idle and transport liveness are separate clocks. Initial idle default is 15 minutes; 0 means no idle sleep. Active lanes still receive independent randomized age rotation, initially 30..60 minutes as policy guidance, with staggered multi-lane replacement.
product_policy.linux_rawip: Final Windows raw-IP server direction is shared WBD TUN + Linux root routing + one WBD-owned host NAT + lease-based demux and source anti-spoof. Per-LiveID netns/veth/double NAT is historical/reference only; VRF/conntrack-zone remains rejected.
product_policy.windows: Wintun/raw L3 remains the product capture path. Underlay escape, IPv6 fail-closed connected interval, deterministic Disconnect/Exit route/DNS/IPv6/firewall cleanup and Npcap release constraints remain mandatory.
product_policy.observability: Keep non-secret correlation IDs, first-boundary markers and counters; do not log usernames/passwords/tickets/resume secrets/identity secrets and do not enable per-packet INFO spam.
